look_here_first: On a flowering plant, photograph the entire scape: ONE tier of three leaflike involucral bracts sits ABOVE the scape midpoint. Then compare multiple basal leaves to that bract tier: all basal leaves are divided differently from the bracts. Flowers alone are not enough.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Herbaceous spring perennial from underground tuber; flowering stalk (scape) with one showy terminal flower.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Basal leaves deeply divided; compare several basal leaves with involucral bracts rather than relying on leaflet outline alone.

key_traits.label: Involucre
key_traits.text: Single tier of three leaflike bracts above the midpoint of the flowering scape; basal leaves dissimilar in division.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Numerous narrow petal-like SEPALS, not true petals; white/pink/purple variation overlaps related species.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Aggregate head of achenes; mature achenes densely woolly; close-up useful as secondary evidence.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: one involucral-bract tier ABOVE scape midpoint

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: all basal leaves divided differently from bracts

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: single terminal flower with petaloid sepals
